attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'I don't expect... to go away' and 'will be' are firm, unhedged statements, so this is a scored forecast. The 'eventually' horizon is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (persistence, plus time savings comparable to history's major labor-saving technologies) is a fair, ordinary reading of 'among the biggest time-savers'. The contract correctly says no finite shortfall can contradict an open-ended forecast.

evidence.note: A June 2026 preprint shows rapid growth in Codex agent use. That bears on adoption and persistence but does not measure net time saved or compare it with history.
METR's February 2026 update finds tentative, unreliable speedups in a narrow developer sample. It neither establishes nor rules out historical-scale savings.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline ('eventually'). The evidence shows growing use of agents and tentative productivity gains, but nothing shows realized time savings on the scale of history's major labor-saving technologies. Nothing permanently rules that outcome out either. The early-resolution rule is not met, so the claim is unresolved.

semantics.note: An observation that mixes a value judgment ('wildly underfunded', with no stated standard) and a figure he hedges explicitly ('if I had to guess maybe 1%, probably less'). The normalisation keeps the hedge.

contract.note: The contract correctly declines to impose a threshold, denominator or period that Marcus did not give. The figure is hedged and the funding judgment has no stated standard.

reviews.rationale: Marcus explicitly hedges the percentage as a guess ('maybe', 'probably'), and policy excludes hedged estimates from scoring. 'Wildly underfunded' is a value judgment with no stated standard. The category, denominator and period are all undefined. The claim is not adjudicable.
